text:
Brendan Gallagher's homecoming has turned into a hard first month. The longtime Canadien, traded to Vancouver for future considerations in June after 911 games in Montreal, has no goals in 18 games, and the Canucks have lost each of the last ten he has played. His last game, against the Rangers, was his shortest of the season at 7.8 minutes. Montreal Hockey Fanatics ran a piece on a "heartbreaking scene" during a Canucks game with the line "It's really a sad end," and the week before, Connor Murphy's chirp at him during an Oilers game went viral, per Markerzone.

Our numbers tell a less final story. He keeps getting to the net: 3.33 expected goals (the quality of his chances) on 22 shots, a rate per minute a bit above last season's. Zero goals on those looks is mostly bad luck, and the Canucks have also scored 5.2 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey had him still driving play last season, with his team creating more chances with him on than with 86% of forwards. At 34, on fourth-line minutes, his runway is shorter. The chances say the goals have not left him yet.
headline: Brendan Gallagher's chances are there, the goals aren't
